chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who believe and do righteous deeds.
Except what slips from them, and He (Exalted) says: 'His authority is only over those who take him as a guardian and those who associate him [with God].'
Thus, the single authority belongs to the monotheists, and the two authorities belong to the polytheists.

key_terms.الْمُشْرِكِينَ: The polytheists (those who associate partners with God)
key_terms.الْمُفْرَدِينَ: The monotheists (those who affirm divine unity exclusively)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Satan's authority over monotheists and polytheists according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifying the theological nuance of Satan's *wilayah* (authority) by distinguishing between absolute dominion over polytheists (*mushrikun*) and limited, conditional authority over monotheists (*muwahhidun*). This distinction underscores the Shia doctrine that while believers are not immune to Satan's whispers, they remain under divine protection unless they voluntarily align themselves with his path, a concept deeply rooted in the exegesis of Surah Yusuf. The narration serves to reassure the faithful of their spiritual resilience while explaining the mechanism of temptation as a test rather than an overpowering force.
